header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (BlueHarbor - Head of MLOps), Diego Ramirez (BlueHarbor - Platform Eng), Priya Shah (BlueHarbor - Security), Tom Keller (BlueHarbor - Product)
summary: Redwood and BlueHarbor agreed on a narrow acceptance test plan for the POC: a three-part benchmark (latency/throughput, quality/regression, and stability under sustained load). Go/no-go thresholds were tentatively set (95th percentile latency <= 180ms for generation baseline, sustained tokens/sec >= 18k for the workload profile, and no greater than 3% regression in quality metrics vs control). Reporting format will be a CSV of run metrics + a Redwood dashboard export and a one-page pass/fail summary. Next steps: Redwood to run baseline, customer to provision test access, follow-up meeting to review results.
topics: Timeline and gating for pilot launch
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Collins: All right, thanks everyone for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Lena Morris: Lena here.
[00:09] Diego Ramirez: Diego.
[00:10] Priya Shah: Priya.
[00:12] Tom Keller: Tom.
[00:14] Avery Collins: Great. Samir, Jordan from our side i think are on too. The goal for today is to lock the success criteria and the acceptance test plan so we can run the POC without back-and-forth.
[00:28] Samir Patel: Yeah, and specifically we want to make sure the go/no-go thresholds are concrete — numbers and artifacts — not just general statements.
[00:36] Lena Morris: Absolutely. We're under a tight timeline, we need to know if Redwood meets our latency and cost envelopes before committing to a larger pilot.
[00:44] Diego Ramirez: I'll also add that our traffic shape is spiky, with bursts lasting up to 10 minutes. So the stability under sustained burst matters.
[00:52] Jordan Li: Noted. For benchmarks we'll include both steady-state and burst profiles. Quick question on the sample dataset: do you want synthetic or production-sampled?
[01:02] Tom Keller: Prefer a sanitized production sample, ideally 100k request traces and 20k prompt items. We can redact PII.
[01:11] Priya Shah: From security side we need to confirm KMS, key rotation, and retention windows. Also please send SOC2 documentation and our legal will want egress details.
[01:22] Avery Collins: We'll include our SOC2 letter and a KMS integration note. For the acceptance criteria, here is our initial proposal: 1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 180ms for our short prompt profile (50-150 tokens), 2) Throughput: sustained >= 18k tokens/sec across the dedicated pool for the steady workload, 3) Quality: automated eval delta not worse than 3% vs your current baseline on rubric X, plus no more than 10% human-rated failures during a 500-sample blind test. Does that map to your needs?
[02:08] Lena Morris: The latency number seems aggressive but within reach if quantization and batching are tuned. Important: define how we measure 95th p — do we include tail from cold starts?
[02:19] Samir Patel: Good call. We'll define two buckets: warm steady-state measurements (exclude cold starts) and end-to-end from first-token for cold-start characterization. Acceptance threshold applies to warm steady-state. Cold-start tail must be documented but not a hard gating metric.
[02:33] Diego Ramirez: For throughput, 18k tokens/sec is close to our calculated need. Can you map that to concurrent request count assumptions?
[02:41] Jordan Li: Yes — that equates roughly to 120 concurrent sessions with median 150 tokens/session and an average generation length of 150 tokens over the 60s window. We'll include a table in the runbook converting tokens/sec to concurrency for different prompt lengths.
[02:56] Tom Keller: On quality — what's the automated metric? BLEU? ROUGE? We primarily care about downstream task accuracy for our ranking model.
[03:04] Samir Patel: We'll run both automated measures (BLEU/ROUGE/F1 depending on task) and a human-label pass. The acceptance is a combined gate: automated delta <= 3% AND human failure rate <= 10%. If automated is slightly worse but human eval is better, we can flag for manual review.
[03:20] Priya Shah: For security, we need cryptographic boundary details. If you use customer-managed keys we need audit logs for all decrypt operations.
[03:29] Avery Collins: Redwood supports KMS integrations — we'll document audit log locations and retention. We'll also provide an export of request-level logs stripped of prompt content for debugging.
[03:40] Lena Morris: Reporting format — what's your standard deliverable? We want raw CSV + summarized dashboard.
[03:46] Avery Collins: Standard deliverable: CSV containing per-request metrics (request id, timestamp, latency p50/p90/p95, tokens generated, model variant, batch size), plus a Redwood dashboard export (PNG + shared dashboard link) and a one-page pass/fail summary that lists whether thresholds were met and highlights regressions.
[04:06] Diego Ramirez: Also include the model/config used per run — e.g., quantized 4-bit variant vs FP16 baseline — we need to be able to reproduce results.
[04:15] Jordan Li: We'll include a run manifest: model version, kernel selection, GPU type, batch settings, cache settings — everything.
[04:21] Tom Keller: Timeline-wise how long until we get a baseline run?
[04:25] Avery Collins: If you drop the sanitized dataset and grant test access by 2026-08-20, we can kick a baseline within 24-48 hours and have initial results by 2026-08-22. We recommend a two-week window for full sanity, regression, and stability testing.
[04:37] Lena Morris: That timeline works. Our legal review might add a day or two for the account.
[04:41] Priya Shah: We'll review the SOC2/KMS notes by 2026-08-24 at latest.
[04:46] Samir Patel: For stability testing we'll run a sustained 2-hour burst run and a 24-hour soak depending on capacity. For the POC gating we'll require the 2-hour burst and 48-hour rolling error rates to be within threshold.
[04:59] Diego Ramirez: On quotas and throttling, how do you handle graceful degradation? If capacity is hit do you fall back to a cheaper model?
[05:06] Avery Collins: We can configure smart routing: fallback to a compatible, lower-cost variant under load or region failover. For the POC we'll keep fallbacks off for baseline runs but document behavior.
[05:16] Tom Keller: Cost estimates please — we need an estimated $/1M tokens for each model variant so we can compare to our budget.
[05:23] Jordan Li: We'll provide a cost table in the runbook: per-token cost at current Redwood rates for hosted vs dedicated reserved throughput assumptions.
[05:31] Lena Morris: Ok, want to confirm acceptance reporting: CSV + dashboard + one-page pass/fail. For the human eval who will do that?
[05:39] Avery Collins: Redwood can run the initial human eval sample (we'll use blinded raters), but you may prefer to run your own. We'll provide the sample set and annotation schema.
[05:48] Priya Shah: For legal egress we need to confirm no prompt content is sent to third-party analytics.
[05:53] Samir Patel: Agreed — we'll document what telemetry is shared.
[05:56] Diego Ramirez: Any competitors' angle? We're also running a Vertex AI quick-check and an OpenAI baseline for quality. We'll need to see comparative numbers.
[06:04] Avery Collins: We'll add a comparative tab in the results export — if you supply those runs or allow Redwood to run them.
[06:10] Lena Morris: Alright, let's recap the go/no-go:
[06:13] Avery Collins: Go/no-go gates: 1) Warm 95p latency <= 180ms for short prompts, 2) Sustained throughput >= 18k tokens/sec under steady workload, 3) Quality automated delta <= 3% and human failure <= 10% on the sample, 4) No critical security flags in KMS/audit review. If any gate fails, outcome is 'no-go' unless a remediation plan is accepted by both parties.
[06:38] Tom Keller: Sounds right. Can you make the pass/fail sheet machine-readable? We'll ingest into our internal tracker.
[06:44] Jordan Li: Yes — CSV + JSON summary object.
[06:48] Priya Shah: Please add a line for compliance artifacts and who owns each.
[06:52] Avery Collins: We'll include a compliance checklist with owners.
[06:55] Diego Ramirez: Final question: if the POC is marginally below thresholds but cost is significantly better, is there room for negotiation?
[07:03] Avery Collins: That's a product-level discussion. For POC acceptance we need to stick to the gates, but the commercial team can discuss tradeoffs for pilot pricing.
[07:11] Lena Morris: OK. Next steps?
[07:13] Avery Collins: Action items captured — I'll send the runbook and S3 link (Avery) by EOD 2026-08-21; Diego will spin up a test account by 2026-08-20; Samir will deliver perf matrix by 2026-08-22. Schedule follow-up on 2026-09-02 to review results.
[07:29] Tom Keller: Thanks everyone.
[07:31] Lena Morris: Thanks.
[07:33] Priya Shah: Thanks, bye.
[07:34] <end>

Notes: transcription had occasional mis-hears (eg. "K V cache" for KV cache, "quantization 4-bit" transcribed sometimes as "quarter bit") and speaker labels are approximate.
